=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Overall:** The package is not "fair and balanced". On liability architecture it is well outside our playbook, and several Seller positions are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. The "negotiated positions" label is also misleading, because we have agreed none of them. I recommend we respond with a full mark-up and do not accept any of these as a starting point.

## 1. Critical issues (liability architecture)

| Issue | Seller | Our position | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | 20% is our **conditional fallback**. It needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none exists. We should not accept it or signal it is acceptable. Counter at 25%. |
| Claims period (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is also a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). Reject. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. Combined with the basket, it would screen out many realistic claims. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, **excess only** | AUD 50,000, **first dollar** once exceeded | 5x higher, and a deductible rather than a tipping basket. This is a large erosion of recoverable value. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. Calling it "administrative simplicity" does not change that it would cap title claims at 20% of the price for 18 months. |
| Fraud carve-out (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) | None. Limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable | Serious. The carve-out is absent, and the wording expressly sweeps in every claim. This cannot be waived, so it is a must-fix. |
| Hidden override (12.3 / 13) | "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate, with no general-regime override | This is the mechanism that would pull title, tax, IP, covenants and payment claims into the general limits. Delete it and replace it with category-specific limits. |

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

- **Deemed disclosure (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2):** The Seller discloses the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. We reject this and require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties. The data room is a large, undifferentiated pool, and general disclosure would let the Seller neutralise warranties without identifying anything.
- **Buyer knowledge (8.3):** The Seller's wording covers matters known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge plus deemed disclosure, which double-counts. Delete it. If any qualifier survives, it must rest on named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **DL 1.4 (non-admission):** This is generally acceptable as a disclosure-letter formality. Make sure it does not undercut the specific indemnities or any covenant to take action (consents, payments, notifications).
- **Housekeeping:** The Disclosure Letter jumps from [1.2] to [1.4], so [1.3] is missing. Ask whether it was removed. Item 11 ("evaluate against the complete agreement") also reads like an attempt to shift the burden to us.

## 3. Deal-specific issues

**Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30%)**
- The Seller Update says the consent is "addressed". The Disclosure Letter (item 2) says no final written consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions has been provided. These are inconsistent.
- Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a consent this material. "Satisfied on delivery" of a consent is also insufficient, because DD-002 clause 11.3 attaches conditions.
- **Require:** an effective written consent **and** evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are met, both as a condition precedent to Completion.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m)**
- The Seller proposes a post-Completion release. The Disclosure Letter (item 3) confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge exists.
- **Require:** a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists, so do not offer it.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000)**
- The funds flow omits them, and the Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller". That does not resolve who funds them.
- The Disclosure Letter does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
- **Require:** a specific line item in the funds flow, or an express Seller-funded mechanism, covering the AUD 420,000 **plus** any triggered on-costs. A silent exclusion is not acceptable.

**Ironquay IP**
- The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment, and the Seller calls it adequate. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, the project materials transfer only on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees.
- **Require:** a broader indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure mechanism.
- The AUD 180,000 in DD-010 is not independently verified in either direction, so do not treat it as confirmed owing or as a cap. We should seek payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". We should not accept that characterisation, because the facts do not establish it either way.
- We also should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any dollar figure.
- **Require:** log preservation, a proper investigation, regular updates to us, and cooperation and consultation rights. Address allocation of consequences through a specific protection that does not depend on a numeric assumption.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- The Seller calls them ordinary-course. The Disclosure Letter (item 8) does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.
- **Do:** assess. Ask for contracts, termination rights and timing. Do not concede ordinary-course status, and do not automatically treat them as Debt or deduct from the price.

**Tax and IP**
- The Seller says they are "settled under the general regime". They are not. Both remain open. Reserve our position, and do not agree they fall under the general caps or any unlimited-liability position.

**Title**
- The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register. That is a supplied internal document and not independent proof.
- **Require:** independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority (for example, ASIC searches, PPSR searches, transfer and issue history, and board and shareholder authority). Title should also have a Fundamental warranty.

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- Neither appears to require consent to the share sale on the face of the disclosure. Confirm against the full documents, and have the Seller warrant that no other consents or notifications are required.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

1. **Do not accept the 20% cap or the 18-month period.** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m and 24 months. Escalate to Amelia Frost only if the team wants to consider a fallback, and note that no authority exists today.
2. **Reset the thresholds** to AUD 5,000 de minimis and an AUD 50,000 basket, with first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
3. **Create a separate Fundamental/Title regime** with a 100% cap, at least 6 years, and exclusion from the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Insert a fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, and delete the "all Claims of any nature" wording and the override in 12.3 / 13.
5. **Reject general disclosure** of the data room and public registers. Require specific disclosure and delete clause 8.3.
6. **Make Bluefen and Riverlark Completion deliverables:** Bluefen consent plus satisfied conditions, and Riverlark payout, direct repayment and releases at Completion.
7. **Add the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs** to the funds flow as a line item, or make them expressly Seller-funded.
8. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** while preserving the SOW3 cure, and treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified.
9. **Handle DD-006 and Sandbar neutrally:** preserve, investigate and require updates on the incident, and assess the renewals, with no assumed outcomes or automatic deductions.
10. **Keep Tax and IP open**, and require independent title verification.
11. **Ask the Seller to confirm** whether Disclosure Letter [1.3] was deleted, and to reconcile the Seller Update's "addressed" statements with the Disclosure Letter, which says Bluefen and Riverlark remain outstanding.

I can draft the mark-up of clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12 and 13 and the Schedule 7 disclosure language, or a short cover note to Seller's counsel rejecting the "negotiated positions" framing.
